findings.finding: LFG rose 26.8% over Q3 (11330p -> 14370p), which on a 14.9% stake worth GEL ~2.5bn (46.9% of portfolio) mechanically adds roughly 11 points to NAV per share, so 3Q26 will print a record NAV of about GEL 196-201 (~GBP 57); but LFG has since fallen 14.4%, so the headline is stale on arrival.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 3Q25 NAV release +0.99%; 1Q26 -3.19%; 2Q26 (NAV +13.1% q-o-q, driven by LFG +22.1%, plus the new GEL 1bn programme) +9.76% - the large move came with the capital-allocation news, not the mechanical NAV
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: LFG trades on the LSE every day and the stake is disclosed, so anyone running the sum has the listed half. What would show it unpriced is the discount having stayed at the June level; instead CGEO is back at its 30-Jun price (4180p) while LFG is +8.6% since then, so the market is not paying for even the current-NAV uplift - the headline may nudge retail holders but the sell-side has it.

findings.finding: The Georgian economy grew 8.0% y-o-y in July 2026 and 7.9% over January-July (Geostat), consistent with GCAP's private large portfolio continuing its run of double-digit revenue growth into Q3 and a positive internal private-portfolio value creation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Private value creation of GEL 239m in 2Q26 (Kroll cycle) vs GEL 78m in 1Q26 (internal); 1Q26 release fell 3.19% - internal-quarter private marks have not lifted the stock
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission and a continuation of a public trend; mostly priced. If the market were pricing an upside private mark the discount would not have widened in October.
findings.independence: Company: 2Q26 large-portfolio revenue +19.1% y-o-y, eighth straight double-digit quarter, https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/georgia-capital--cgeo/half-year-financial-report/9702442

findings.finding: Chairman/CEO Irakli Gilauri sold 175,000 shares for GBP 7.59m between 28 Aug and 2 Sep 2026 (holding 2.65m, voting rights 5.19% -> 4.86%) ahead of the Q3 closed period, partly offset by a NED buying 2,000 shares at GBP 44.65 on 24 Sep.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none observed on a results day; the stock rose to 4725p within two weeks of the sale
findings.why_not_priced: Public since 2 Sep and two months old; mostly priced. It is filed because it is a sourced fact on the name, but a reaction on the day would need the release or webinar to touch it.

findings.finding: The discount to NAV has widened: about 16.6% at 30 June (4180p vs GBP 50.10), about 18% at 30 September (4705p vs an estimated ~GBP 57.5), and about 22-23% now against an estimated current NAV of ~GBP 54 after LFG's October fall, with the irrevocable buyback buying 10,000 shares a day through the closed period.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2Q26 release +9.76% when the company addressed capital return (new GEL 1bn programme); the company itself wrote in August that a narrower discount makes new investments relatively more attractive, so a wider discount argues for buybacks again
findings.why_not_priced: The NAV estimate is this hunter's arithmetic, not a published number; with two analysts and no published Q3 NAV, the widening is visible only to someone who runs the sum. If the market had priced the NAV, CGEO would have tracked LFG's +8.6% since June rather than sitting flat at 4180p.
